basics.name: Muhammad Bilal Azam
basics.label: Graduate Research Assistant | PhD Candidate in Physics
basics.summary: PhD candidate in Physics at Illinois Institute of Technology and Graduate Research Assistant at Argonne National Laboratory. Member of the DUNE Collaboration, specializing in AI/ML-based neutrino event reconstruction, simulation, and analysis for the DUNE Near Detector Prototype (2×2).

education.summary: Doctor of Philosophy in Physics. Thesis supervisor: Prof. Dr. Zelimir Djurcic. Research on AI/ML-based neutrino reconstruction and DUNE 2×2 data analysis.
Master of Science in Physics. Thesis title: Dark Energy in Causal Set Theory. Thesis supervisor: Prof. Dr. Maqbool Ahmed.
Bachelors of Science in Mathematics and Physics.

work.name: Argonne National Laboratory
work.summary: Detector development and data analysis for the Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment (DUNE).
highlights: Photon Detection Calibration System: design, simulation, and testing of photon detection calibration systems for DUNE detector prototypes.

Neutrino Event Generator and Multiplicity Studies: charged-current multiplicity studies comparing measured data with neutrino generator simulations, to select the optimal generator for future DUNE analyses.

Event Selection Optimization and AI/ML Reconstruction: tuning simulated events, optimizing neutrino event selection, and enhancing AI/ML-based particle reconstruction using HPC workflows and hyperparameter optimization, including systematic uncertainty studies.

work.name: Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS)
work.summary: Learning How to Learn (Adaptation Project): adapted and translated course assessments from English to Urdu for the Coursera course by Barbara Oakley and Dr. Terrence Sejnowski.

work.name: Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS)
work.summary: Everpresent Lambda in the Closed Universe: studied the effects of strong and weak curvature on dark energy behavior, developed a formalism for fluctuating Λ including metric functional derivatives, and worked on incorporating CMB anisotropies into the model.

work.name: Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS)
work.summary: Dark Energy in Causal Set Theory: addressed the fine-tuning and naturalness problems of dark energy in a spherical topology universe using unimodular gravity and causal set theory, based on the fluctuating cosmological constant model of Ahmed et al. (2004), under the supervision of Dr. Maqbool Ahmed.

projects.name: Exotic Matter and Search for Magnetic Monopoles (MoEDAL at CERN)
projects.summary: Discussed exotic matter and its role in explaining non-baryonic physics beyond the Standard Model, with a focus on magnetic monopoles via Dirac and 't Hooft treatments and their experimental search at CERN through the MoEDAL experiment.

projects.name: What is the meaning of "same" and "different" in context of measurements?
projects.summary: Designed and conducted an experiment using conical pendulums to study the agreement between theoretical predictions and experimental results.

projects.name: Solar Neutrino Problem
projects.summary: Studied the solar neutrino problem and its theoretical and experimental resolution, with detailed discussions on neutrino flavor mixing via the PMNS matrix and two-neutrino mixing approximations used in oscillation data analysis.

projects.name: Majorana Fermions and Topological Superconductors
projects.summary: Studied topological superconductors and their connection to Majorana fermions, including a comparison with Dirac fermions and a pedagogical review of topological superconductivity. Detailed the Bogoliubov–de Gennes (BdG) Hamiltonian via mean-field theory, with emphasis on the spinless one-dimensional p-wave topological superconductor case.

projects.name: Study of Optical Properties of Isotropic Materials by Reflection SE
projects.summary: Studied isotropic thin films by obtaining ellipsometric parameters Ψ and Δ using J.A. Woollam's Alpha-SE Ellipsometer, extracted n, k, and d, and verified the complex reflection coefficient ρ using MATLAB. Also cross-validated the refractive index of glass thin films via Alpha-SE Ellipsometry and Michelson Interferometry.
